Right now i have to scan markets manually for good trade setups.  I need to place trades at times that make sense.  when Im at work I can't place any trades or do any research.  I want the scanner to find the setups for me.  the high probability ones.  it can notify me and I can have it place the trade for me in one click.  I can also set up the bot to autonomously buy and sell for me.  just as if I were to place the trades manually.  This takes the emotions out of the trades and sticks to a system
• Name the markets and instruments: e.g. 'US equities and options' or 'crypto spot on Binance' — the scanner, broker API, and market hours all depend on this.
• Define 'high probability setup' concretely: which patterns or indicators (e.g. breakout above 20-day high with volume spike, RSI divergence), so the scanner has testable rules.
• State which broker or exchange the bot will place trades through, and confirm it has an API that supports one-click and autonomous order placement.
• Specify how notifications reach you at work: push notification, SMS, or Telegram — and that the one-click trade must work from a phone.
• Add risk controls to the 'why now': max position size, stop-loss per trade, and a daily loss limit that halts the bot, since it will trade unattended.

• Mention timeframe: is this scanning intraday setups every few minutes, or end-of-day swing setups once daily? This changes the architecture a lot.

• Core thesis (lead with this): SniperSight4 turns discretionary market-structure reading into an objective, testable process. A deterministic, rules-based engine maps structure (swings, ranges, liquidity levels) — same chart in, same map out, every time. On top of that map, it flags setups matching defined playbooks and scores each signal with a plain-language, explainable rationale. Strategy validation (backtest → paper) is the trust engine; automated live execution is the endgame, unlocked only for strategies that survive validation. v1 promise: 'see the structure, trust the signal' — not 'let the bot trade for you.'

Strong trend → Pullback or trend-following strategy.
Range → Adaptive Grid Strategy.
Breakout → Breakout strategy.
Trend exhaustion → Reversal strategy.
• Primary (launch): discretionary retail/prop traders who already trade a defined playbook. Today they mark structure by hand in TradingView, journal in spreadsheets, and suffer three pains: inconsistent structure reads day-to-day, no statistical proof their setups have an edge, and rule-breaking under pressure. Jobs: (1) get one objective structure map per chart, (2) backtest/forward-test my playbook against that map, (3) get flagged live when my setup appears — with the rationale spelled out. Secondary (post-validation): the same user graduating to guarded auto-execution. Explicit non-users: signal-seekers without a system, HFT/quant funds, options-flow day-gamblers.

scope.response: • V1 is a deterministic market-intelligence engine: market-structure analysis, setup detection, strategy backtesting, and paper trading with explainable trade reasoning. Markets: cryptocurrency and stocks only. Non-goals for V1: (1) No live/automated trade execution — paper trades only, to validate strategy performance and risk management before any real capital is used. (2) No social or copy trading — leaderboards and strategy sharing deferred until the core engine is proven. (3) No options or other derivatives. (4) No asset classes beyond crypto and equities (no forex, futures).

platform.response:
the goal is to have it on the desktop as a launchable app but eventually i want to be on mobile and end game an apk
• Distribution: installable desktop app first (Windows priority), mobile later, endgame an Android APK. To make that path cheap, the UI is a web-tech shell (React/TypeScript + TradingView lightweight-charts) packaged with Tauri — Tauri 2 also builds Android, so the same UI codebase becomes the APK later. The analysis engine (market-structure mapping, backtester, paper-trade simulator) is a Python FastAPI service the UI only ever talks to over HTTP/WebSocket — on desktop it runs as a bundled local sidecar process; on mobile it will be the hosted version of the same service. Storage: SQLite locally for V1 (upgrade path to Postgres/Timescale when hosted). Market data via read-only exchange/provider APIs. No order-placement credentials anywhere.

architecture.response: • Pipeline: market-data importer → per-class fact engines (swing / structure / zone / liquidity / regime; one engine per class) → fact store → strategy engine → risk authority → execution sim (no live orders in v1). The fact store owns all derived-fact state — engines write, nothing else does; the strategy reads only through an as_of-cursored query. Risky seam: the engine↔store schema and the store↔strategy query contract — get them wrong and the chart and the bot disagree on what a 'level' is; both are validated packets from day one. Replay is the store itself: every fact is append-only with market_time, confirmed_at, invalidated_at, algo_version, so any past state reconstructs by querying as_of=T — no re-derivation, no repainting.

delivery.response: • Milestones gated on the risky seam, one vertical slice at a time. M1: importer + fact store + swing engine only, end-to-end — gate: re-running the engine over identical data yields byte-identical facts, and as_of=T reconstructs any past state with zero re-derivation. M2: remaining engines (structure, zone, liquidity, regime) + chart overlay that reads the exact same as_of query the bot uses — gate: chart and bot provably agree on every level. M3: strategy engine + risk authority + execution sim — gate: a full backtest rides the confirmed_at cursor with an automated no-lookahead check (no fact consumed before its confirmed_at). M4: validation harness — walk-forward runs and algo_version A/B comparisons — gate: two algo_versions coexist in the store and are queryable side by side.

look.response: • Tactical HUD aesthetic — glass-cockpit avionics meets a modern trading terminal (refs: EVE Online HUD, Tron-style FUI, TradingView dark density). Near-black base with high-contrast accent pair (e.g., cyan for structure/info, amber-red for risk/execution). Glow is signal, not decoration: reserved for live states — setup validated, order working, alert firing. Dense but calm: strict grid, consistent card/panel chrome, generous spacing inside panels, monospaced numerics. Chart-first center stage, instrument/status rails on edges, everything findable in ≤2 clicks. Motion minimal and purposeful (state transitions only). Consistency enforced via a small token set: 2 accents, 3 surface levels, 1 glow treatment.
